overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 16
overview.text: In this lesson, you will solve compound inequalities algebraically and graph their solution sets on a real number line. You will observe that 'and' inequalities typically yield bounded segments ($a < x < b$), while 'or' inequalities often produce disjoint rays pointing in opposite directions.
outcomes: Solve compound linear inequalities joined by 'and' or 'or'.
Graph bounded intervals (conjunctions) and disjoint rays (disjunctions) accurately on a number line.
Translate compound inequalities into interval notation.
overview.teacherInsight: Make sure students recognize shorthand compound notation: $-3 < 2x + 1 \le 7$ is shorthand for '$-3 < 2x + 1$ AND $2x + 1 \le 7$'. Never write disjoint 'or' statements in chained notation like $x < 2 \text{ or } x > 5$.

content.html:
Anatomy of Compound Inequality Graphs

Bounded Interval ("And")

$$-2 < x \le 4$$

Represents the intersection of $x > -2$ and $x \le 4$. The graph is a line segment between -2 (open circle) and 4 (closed dot).

Disjoint Rays ("Or")

$$x \le -1 \quad \text{or} \quad x > 3$$

Represents the union of two separate rays pointing outward in opposite directions.

vocabulary.definition: An inequality formed by joining two individual inequalities with the connective word 'and' or 'or'.
A continuous interval of real numbers with finite endpoints on both sides, e.g., (a, b] or [a, b].
Two sets that have no elements in common (their intersection is empty).

practiceQuestions.question: Solve the compound inequality $9 + 2x < 17 \text{ or } 7 - 4x < -9$:
practiceQuestions.explanation:
From the official Eureka Math Exit Ticket Key:
$9 + 2x < 17 \implies 2x < 8 \implies x < 4$
$7 - 4x < -9 \implies -4x < -16 \implies x > 4$
The union of $x < 4$ and $x > 4$ covers every number on the number line except 4, written as $x \ne 4$.

practiceQuestions.question: Solve the double inequality $6 \le \frac{x}{2} \le 11$ for $x$:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Multiply each part of the compound inequality by 2: $6 \times 2 \le \left(\frac{x}{2}\right) \times 2 \le 11 \times 2 \implies 12 \le x \le 22$.

exitTicket.title: Lesson 16 Exit Ticket: Solving and Graphing Inequalities Joined by 'And' or 'Or'
exitTicket.prompt: Solve each compound inequality for x, and graph the solution on a number line: (a) 9 + 2x < 17 or 7 - 4x < -9; (b) 6 <= x/2 <= 11. Give an example of a compound inequality separated by 'or' that has a solution of all real numbers.
exitTicket.solution:
1) 9 + 2x < 17 => 2x < 8 => x < 4. 7 - 4x < -9 => -4x < -16 => x > 4. Combined: x < 4 or x > 4, which is equivalent to x != 4 (all real numbers except 4).
2) 6 <= x/2 <= 11 => multiply by 2: 12 <= x <= 22.
3) Example with all real numbers: x > 0 or x < 2.

guidedExercises.title: Example 1: Solving Compound Multi-Step Inequalities
guidedExercises.scaffolding: Solve each inequality independently, then determine the intersection of their solution sets.

steps.label: Find intersection of $x \ge 2$ and $x < 5$
steps.explanation: Includes 2 (closed circle) and goes up to 5 (open circle).

guidedExercises.commonPitfall: Forgetting that 'and' requires both conditions to hold. If you take the union instead of intersection, you would incorrectly include numbers outside $[2, 5)$.
